body:
Thanks for having a look, @Mickeon.

> We need a general rule as to what keywords _should be_ for classes.

Agreed.
Both in terms of formatting, but also in terms of the choice of keywords.

For formatting, I'm a fan of copying the original member's formatting (so PascalCase for classes, snake_case for methods, etc.). Haven't followed this here since other class keywords don't currently do it, but might be worth a discussion.

Regarding content, I don't personally have a strong opinion (besides "more is better" to aid discoverability). You're free to open a proposal discussing the matter, or we can bikeshed on PRs like this to find something we're both happy with ^^

> just tangentially related to the class's subject (such as `vr`). 

I'd argue users from varying background would expect finding virtual reality nodes in Godot by searching for `VR` moreso than `XR`. Though an argument could be made to remove it from the non-node classes that I've added it to.

> Also worth keeping in mind is that these terms are not localized [...] keywords like `vertical` and `horizontal` are not relevant in other languages.

But class/method/member names are also not localized, so users searching for classes/methods/etc. (may it be in F1 or in create dialog) will *always* have to write English strings to find things.
If I want something vertical, I won't type it in my native language because I know that Godot names its things in English.

If you're referring to the documentation pages being localized (and thus searching on docs.gd.org takes keywords into account), I can see that. Not sure if the chance of creating a false positive (the user searches for something unrelated which just happens to overlap with an English keyword) is worse, if it helps discovery of things with an arguably bad name.
